quotes.file: རྒྱལ་ཚབ་དར་མ་རིན་ཆེན་_རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན།.txt
quotes.why: The opening of the passage the paragraph cites as རྣམ་བཤད་ལས — Gyaltsab Je's own words, which Chökyi Gyaltsen reproduces almost verbatim.

quotes.file: རྒྱལ་ཚབ་དར་མ་རིན་ཆེན་_རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན།.txt
quotes.why: The close of Gyaltsab Je's passage: the Buddha-eye, even in its approximating form, makes the bodhisattva self-directed in practice — the purpose the paragraph then turns into a syllogism.

quotes.file: འཕགས་པ་གྲོལ་སྡེ་_ཉི་ཁྲི་སྣང་བ།.txt
quotes.why: Ārya Vimuktisena's summary of the ten instructions: the Indian origin of the claim that the five eyes are the cause of proceeding without dependence on others. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: བྱམས་པ་མགོན་པོ་_མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན།.txt
quotes.why: The root verse whose words སྤྱན་ལྔ and མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི། ། ཡོན་ཏན་དྲུག are the lemmas of this paragraph and the next. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: སེང་གེ་བཟང་པོ་_འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ།.txt
quotes.text: ཤའི་དང་། རྣམ་པར་སྨིན་པ་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་ལྷའི་དང་། ཤེས་རབ་དང་ཆོས་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་གྲངས་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་དངོས་པོ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པ་དང་། སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་འཆི་འཕོ་བ་དང་། སྐྱེ་བ་དང་། ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་རྣམ་པར་མི་རྟོག་པ་དང་། འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག་ཐམས་ཅད་རྟོགས་པ་དང་། ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་བྱང་ཆུབ་པའི་ཡུལ་ཅན་རྣམས
quotes.why: Haribhadra's entire gloss on the five eyes: their five objects and nothing more — no statement of purpose, no grades of the fleshly eye, no discussion of the gods. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04020_THEG PA CHEN PO MDO SDE'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Mahāyana Sūtrālaṃkāra Nāma Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (Tōh. 4020), the four verses on the conditions for practice — end of the first and the whole of the second.
quotes.why: The canonical text of the first two verses the paragraph cites from མདོ་སྡེའི་རྒྱན — note the root text reads ཡོན་ཏན་ལྡན where the yig cha has ཡོ་བྱད་ལྡན.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04020_THEG PA CHEN PO MDO SDE'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Mahāyana Sūtrālaṃkāra Nāma Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (Tōh. 4020), the third and fourth of the same four verses.
quotes.why: The canonical text of the verses on right aspiration and past merit; the kārikā here reads ཡང་དག་གཏོད་པ where the yig cha, and the bhāṣya, read ཡང་དག་སྨོན་ལམ.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Sūtrālaṃkāra-vyākhyā (Tōh. 4026), on the first of the four verses.
quotes.why: The Indian bhāṣya itself reads the four Sūtrālaṃkāra verses as the four wheels — the link that lets the paragraph set the Friendly Letter's four wheels beside them. Found by reading the pack's canonical lead.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The source of the paragraph's five-part gloss of the aspiration verse — and the witness that reads ཆོག་པར་མི་འཛིན, the opposite of the yig cha's ཆོག་པར་འཛིན.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 3 (MI)/TD04034-1_MDO SDE RGYAN GYI 'GREL BSHAD (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vṛttibhāṣya)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Sthiramati, Sūtrālaṃkāra-vṛttibhāṣya (Tōh. 4034), on the third verse.
quotes.why: Sthiramati's subcommentary agrees with the bhāṣya: the good ངེས་འབྱུང is not being satisfied with a little virtue. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: རྗེ་བཙུན་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་མཚན་_སྦྱོར་ལམ་གྱི་སྤྱི་དོན།.txt
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen uses the same Sūtrālaṃkāra verse elsewhere, in the same vocabulary of མཐུན་རྐྱེན and འགལ་རྐྱེན, as the conditions for calm abiding.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā (Kangyur, Nyi khri vol. 1), the five eyes.
quotes.why: The sūtra passage behind བྱང་ཆེན་ཤའི་མིག་གི and ཤའི་སྤྱན་གྱི་སྐབས་སུ། དཔག་ཚད་བརྒྱ་མཐོང་བ — a graded series, which is what the paragraph's question is about. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā (Kangyur, Nyi khri vol. 1), the divine eye.
quotes.why: The sūtra names the five Pure Abodes by name among the gods who cannot know a bodhisattva's divine eye — which is what generates the paragraph's objection. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: མཆེ་བའི་སྡེ་_འབུམ་པའི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ།.txt
quotes.citation: འབུམ་པའི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ། (Bṛhaṭṭīkā, ascribed here to Daṃṣṭrāsena), on the bodhisattva's fleshly eye.
quotes.why: The Indian source of the paragraph's answer that the grades of seeing follow the grades of ground and quality, word for word.

quotes.file: མཆེ་བའི་སྡེ་_འབུམ་པའི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ།.txt
quotes.citation: འབུམ་པའི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ། on the bodhisattva's divine eye.
quotes.why: The Indian source of the paragraph's reason for why the gods cannot know a bodhisattva's divine eye — with no mention of the Pure Abodes.

quotes.file: ཙོང་ཁ་པ་བློ་བཟང་གྲགས་པ་_ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་སྟོད་ཆ།.txt
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's sentence, which the paragraph's first qualm-and-answer restates almost verbatim; Tsongkhapa names the འབུམ་གྱི་གནོད་འཇོམས as his source.

quotes.file: ཙོང་ཁ་པ་བློ་བཟང་གྲགས་པ་_ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་སྟོད་ཆ།.txt
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's own addition to the Indian gloss, and the source of the paragraph's last objection — but he resolves it by śrāvaka āryas, where Chökyi Gyaltsen names Mahāyāna āryas.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/KUN MKHYEN CHOS 'BYOR DPAL BZANG_KUNKYEN CHUNJOR PELSANG/S00999E_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN 'GREL PA 'GREL BSHAD DANG BCAS PA'I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA BSAM 'PHEL DBANG GI RGYAL PO_'The Lord of Lords among Wish-Giving Gems,' being a Detailed Commentary to both the Commentary and Subcommentary _unicode.txt
quotes.why: Kunkyen Chöjor Pelsang's purpose-syllogism, which the paragraph's དོན་བསྡུ་ན section follows almost clause for clause, together with the same Friendly Letter and Sūtrālaṃkāra citations. Found by reading the pack's canonical-sources lead.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/KUN MKHYEN CHOS 'BYOR DPAL BZANG_KUNKYEN CHUNJOR PELSANG/S00999E_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN 'GREL PA 'GREL BSHAD DANG BCAS PA'I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA BSAM 'PHEL DBANG GI RGYAL PO_'The Lord of Lords among Wish-Giving Gems,' being a Detailed Commentary to both the Commentary and Subcommentary _unicode.txt
quotes.why: The same five-part gloss of the aspiration verse that the paragraph gives, in the earlier text — reading ཆོག་པར་མི་འཛིན, with the Indian commentaries and against every edition of the yig cha.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/SE RA RJE BTZUN CHOS KYI RGYAL MTSAN_SERA JETSUN CHUKYI GYELTSEN (1469-1546)/SPYI DON_OVERVIEW/S06814-1_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA’I RGYAN ‘GREL PA DANG BCAS PA’I RNAM BSHAD RNAM PA GNYIS KYI DKA’ BA’I GNAD GSAL BAR BYED PA LEGS BSHAD SKAL BZANG KLU DBANG GI ROL MTSO_ The Excellent Explanation, a Sea of Sport for Those Fort_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྗེ་བཙུན་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་མཚན། སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། Sungbum edition (S06814-1), the same passage as this paragraph.
quotes.why: A second edition of this yig cha with the same reading ཆོག་པར་འཛིན, showing the missing negation is not peculiar to the edition this analysis translates.
